Research ran to completion: notes.md carries an authoritative RESEARCH COMPLETE block (amended, superseding an earlier one whose minute stamps had drifted ahead of the wall clock), so truncated is false. Five distinct symbols were captured across nine candidates.jsonl lines — CAG, MU and LCII were each re-captured after research audited claimed conviction against the distinct-evidence-kind count, and the last entry per symbol is what is published here.

ARITHMETIC RECOMPUTED AT SYNTHESIS, not carried over. All five quotes were re-fetched and match the candidates exactly. NKE 2.080 R:R on a 2.75 ATR stop; MU 2.289 on 2.56 ATR; GDX 2.276 on 1.83 ATR. All clear the 2.0 swing floor and their asset-class ATR stop floors (2.0 stock, 1.8 ETF). Edge over the 1/(1+R:R) random-walk baseline is +7.5, +11.6 and +7.5 points respectively.

TWO THINGS THE READER SHOULD BE SUSPICIOUS OF. First, the three ratios cluster at 2.08-2.29 against a 2.0 floor, which is the signature of targets fitted to clear the bar. Against that: every level traces to fetched structure rather than a round number — MU's entry band is its SMA20 (994.14) down to its SMA50 (941.62) with the target at the 1255.00 range high; GDX's entry is a three-point shelf (09-24 low 90.85, 09-16 low 91.19, SMA50 90.01) with the target at the 08-28 high of 104.78; NKE's trigger is its SMA20 (37.0985) above a 35.2159 range low. Second, GDX's stop is 1.83 ATR against an 1.8 ETF floor — it passes, but only just, and it is the thinnest margin in the report.

WHY ONLY FIVE, AND WHY THAT IS NOT THIN EFFORT. Only one (GDX) is a genuinely new position; two are conditional re-levellings marked wait, and two are exits of open losers. The three lanes that normally carry a weekend run all failed for documented reasons: no priceable Kalshi macro market (every quote field null unauthenticated, so three event-contract rows in the book could not be re-priced), no crypto OHLCV from any source (hence no ATR, hence no compliant stop), and bitcoin failing the R:R floor anyway at 1.55 via IBIT and 0.83 via /MBT. Six further real setups — MCHP, TXN, CMCSA, CNXC, IDT, ACN — were worked to a conclusion and rejected on their merits; research explicitly declined a 2.84 R:R on MCHP that existed only by passing a nine-day-old low off as a bear case.

RANKING NOTE. All five score conviction 4, and the two exits have no reward-to-risk to rank on, so they sort by catalyst proximity — both are Monday-open actions, which is why they head the list. Among the three entries R:R governs (MU 2.289, GDX 2.276, NKE 2.080); MU and GDX are 0.013 apart and effectively tied, so proximity broke it. Ranks 3 and 5 are marked WAIT and are not to be entered Monday morning.

Index levels for today are UNKNOWN and none is stated — spx, ndx, dow, rut, vix, ES/NQ, DXY, us10y_yield, gold and wti all failed across every source, so sector ETF proxies carry the market context instead. === RED TEAM 2026-09-26 ===

Five ideas reviewed. Every level was recomputed from freshly fetched bars rather than read off the report. Two structural findings come before the individual verdicts, because both would have cost the reader more than any single idea.

FINDING 1 — EVERY `earnings_date` WARNING IN THIS REPORT IS A VALIDATOR BUG, NOT A REPORT ERROR. validate_report.py flagged CAG, MU and NKE as claiming an earnings catalyst while "not on the fetched calendar". The cause is scripts/validate_report.py:587, which calls md.earnings(45): that 45-day window overflows finnhub's 1500-row cap and silently returns the FAR TAIL of the range — 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-10 — so it contains no near-dated earnings at all and cannot confirm any company reporting in the next five weeks. Re-fetched at 21 and 7 days, all three dates confirm exactly, with the estimates matching the report: NKE 2026-09-28 (EPS est 0.4444 / rev est $11.45B), CAG 2026-09-29 (0.2842 / $2.61B), MU 2026-09-30 after the close (32.3202 / $52.24B). All three earnings claims are VERIFIED and none should be discounted. The NKE warning still standing in its validation block below is this bug, not a finding. Recorded rather than patched — logic changes need a test, the same reason the research phase left the market_data.py events bug alone.

FINDING 2 — THIS PIPELINE CANNOT EXPRESS "CLOSE AN OPEN POSITION", AND BOTH EXITS WERE ABOUT TO BE LOST. The CAG and LCII exits are the best-reasoned items in the report and both are time-critical Monday-open actions, but as recommendations they fail in two directions at once. (a) publish_sheets.merge_report keys live positions on (symbol, direction) and positions_from_report filters only on catalyst.wait, so a `direction: sell` exit does not close the open `buy` — it appends a brand new short at the exit price with target and stop both null, a position nothing can ever close. This is not hypothetical: the 2026-09-08 NKE "exit call at 38.40" is sitting in state/open_positions.json right now as an open short created exactly this way, which is why today's NKE idea had to spend a paragraph reconciling two open rows. (b) validate_report.py has no exit concept at all, so an exit with no target or stop always fails direction_consistency, risk_reward and stop_distance — and phase 2d --enforce demotes every failure to the watchlist under the note "Demoted by validation: entry or target is missing". Left alone, the two most actionable items this morning would have reached the reader as "not yet actionable" rows with an unreadable reason. So the red team moved both to the watchlist deliberately, with the full instruction, the levels and the accepted cost written out in plain language. THE PLACEMENT IS A PIPELINE LIMITATION, NOT A DOWNGRADE: both exits are endorsed and both are to be done at Monday's open. The fix belongs in the pipeline — an exit needs its own direction or a close_position field — and needs a test, so it was not attempted here.

MU CUT to the watchlist. The 2.29:1 is a fitted number. The standing setup was 960 / 870 / 1140 = exactly 2.00:1; with the entry raised to the 20-day at 994 and the stop to 880, that same 1140 target yields 1.28:1 and fails, and only a target moved out to 1255.00 — the extreme of the 180-day range — restores 2.29:1. Compounding it, the edge is already priced by the idea's own evidence — 91.4% sell-side bullish share, classed deteriorating, after +17.1% in eight sessions into the print — and that bearish positioning item was nonetheless counted as one of the three confirmations paying for conviction 4. Fifth publication in ten days, four prior non-fills. The date and estimates are confirmed and the memory thesis may be right; it is priced.

GDX KEPT at rank 1, stop widened. The best-anchored idea in the report: every level traced to a fetched bar, including the target's anchor — the 08-28 high of 104.78 — which was re-fetched and confirmed, with the 104.40 target sitting just inside it. Acted on the stop_distance warning rather than noting it: 85.40 was 1.83 ATR, clearing the 1.8 ETF floor by a hair and sitting under the 2.25 ATR band where all ten of this report's first stop-outs clustered. The stop is widened to 84.87, a full 2.00 ATR, WITHOUT touching the target — so reward-to-risk falls from 2.28:1 to 2.09:1 and still clears the floor, confirmed by re-running the validator rather than by hand. That is the whole margin this idea has, and the reader should know it: at 2.25 ATR the stop would be 84.08 and the ratio 1.85:1, which fails, so 2.00 ATR is the most survivable stop compatible with the 2.0 floor. win_probability left at 0.38, since a wider stop can only reduce the chance of being hit. One figure corrected: key_risk claimed GLD fell 20.06% from its high against GDX's 20.74%; the fetched figure is 22.82%, so the miners have so far fallen LESS than the metal, which supports the thesis rather than qualifying it. One exposure the idea never screened, now in key_risk: GDX is a basket and its holdings report Q3 inside the 2026-11-13 time stop.

NKE KEPT at rank 2, CONVICTION CUT 4 to 3. Levels verified: SMA20 37.0985 as the trigger, SMA50 39.6824, range low 35.2159 — which is the 09-25 low, made on the most recent bar — range high 68.49, ATR14 0.9099, stop 2.75 ATR, earnings 09-28 confirmed. The conditional structure is why it survives: the entry sits above the market on a post-print reclaim, so the falling-knife case never fills. What is not paid for is conviction 4. Of three evidence kinds, the dated_catalyst is the print the idea explicitly waits out rather than a confirmation of direction; the positioning is insider buys from 2026-04-10 and 04-13, five and a half months old and 15-18% underwater, against revisions still deteriorating (buy 12 to 8, sell 2 to 3); and the technical_level is a range low set yesterday. Separately, the 42.30 target's only stated anchor is those insider fill prices, and an insider's fill price is not resistance — verified supply sits in between at the 39.76 (08-28) and 39.88 (08-31) highs on the 50-day, where a target would give 1.03:1. The target was left alone rather than rescued or trimmed, but that dependency is now in key_risk.

A CAUTION THAT APPLIES TO BOTH SURVIVORS. The headline reward-to-risk is entry-to-target, but both plans trim before the target, so neither intends to realise it: GDX blends to about 1.66R (a third at 96.29 for 0.80R, two thirds at 104.40 for 2.09R) and NKE to about 1.56R (half at 39.70 for 1.04R, half at 42.30 for 2.08R). Sizing off the headline ratio means sizing off a number the plan does not aim at. Not grounds to cut either idea, and both still beat their break-even on the blend, but the ratios should be read with it.

CORRELATION. Four of the five rows run on one factor. Both exits close consumer longs against the same 10y-at-5.18% backdrop, GDX needs the real rate to stay thin, and NKE is credit-sensitive discretionary — so a long end that keeps rising hurts both survivors together while vindicating both exits. The two survivors are not one position in two tickers (gold miners and a broken consumer brand are genuinely different businesses), so neither is cut for it, but they are less independent than a count of two suggests.

NET: one idea cut (MU), two exits moved to the watchlist with their instructions intact and explicitly endorsed, one conviction cut (NKE 4 to 3), one stop widened (GDX 85.40 to 84.87, ratio 2.28 to 2.09), five figures corrected across four ideas, and every earnings warning in the report traced to a validator bug and dismissed with evidence. Two recommendations stand — GDX rank 1 and NKE rank 2 — and nothing in this report, recommendation or exit, is actionable before Monday 2026-09-28.

market_context.summary: A narrow tape against a hostile rate backdrop. The index and tech proxies sit within about a point of their highs and above both moving averages (SPY -1.03% off its high, XLK -1.24%), while the consumer complex is broadly broken beneath both — XLY -9.52%, XRT -11.82%, XLP -8.88%. Discretionary and staples falling together is a read on the consumer, not a rotation between them. Rates are a bear steepener: the 10y at 5.18% is 130bp ABOVE the 3.88% policy rate and the 10y-2y spread widened to +0.36 from +0.31, so the long end is pricing term premium and inflation risk rather than growth, with monthly CPI at +0.40% (~4.9% annualized) doing nothing to argue otherwise. That combination is hostile to long-duration equity proxies and to credit-sensitive big-ticket discretionary — which is the backdrop for both exits in this report. US index levels could not be fetched from any source today and none is stated.

catalyst.event: September CPI released Tue 2026-10-14 08:30 ET (BLS schedule, fetched), then the FOMC decision 2026-10-28 14:00 ET (Fed calendar, fetched). Gold miners trade off real rates, and these are the two dated events that move the real rate inside this horizon.
catalyst.action: accumulate the 90.00-92.20 shelf BEFORE the 10-14 print rather than chasing the reaction; trim a third into the 20-day if it gets there first. Do not add on the print itself.

recommendations.thesis: The miners are outperforming the metal and that gap is operating leverage showing up in the tape: GDX has beaten GLD by 15.32% over three months and 14.52% over six, and GDX at 92.87 is above its 50-day at 90.01 while GLD at 393.41 is below both its own averages. Cost lines are fixed while the realised gold price is not, so a flat-to-firm metal still expands miner margins — which is why the divergence persists rather than closing. With CPI running +0.40% month-over-month against a 3.88% policy rate, the real rate that has been the drag on this complex is thin, and the 10-14 print is the next dated test of it. Entry is a defined three-point support shelf, not a discount off the last print.
recommendations.key_risk: GDX is a basket of leveraged operators, so the same operating leverage runs in reverse — a renewed leg down in gold takes the miners further than the metal, and GDX fell 20.74% from its own range high while GLD fell 20.06% from its. The specific danger is the long end: if the 10y keeps climbing from 5.18% without CPI accelerating, the real rate rises and the whole complex de-rates regardless of mine economics, which is the mechanism that produced this drawdown in the first place.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that one month already contradicts three: GDX is -9.32% over the last month and has lagged GLD by 2.70% over that window, so the outperformance I am buying may be in the process of unwinding rather than continuing, and buying a pullback in a complex 20% off its high is the classic mistake. I take the point seriously enough to let it set the structure: the entry is capped at 92.20 and explicitly voided by a close under 90.00, so if the one-month trend is the real signal the idea simply stops out or never fills rather than being averaged down. The counter-evidence is that the one-month lag is a pullback INTO the 50-day while the three- and six-month leads are moves ABOVE it — the shorter window is noise around a level the longer windows built.

recommendations.thesis: Update to the 2026-08-17 long at 40.75 and the 2026-09-08 exit call at 38.40: hold the remaining long through Monday's print, do not add to it, and treat any new risk as the conditional entry below. NKE has beaten a steadily cut bar by 50.2%, 22.9% and 39.2% in the last three quarters while sell-side bullish share fell to 39.1%, and it goes into Monday 2026-09-28 priced 1.52% above its 35.2159 range low and 47.8% below its high. The trade is not the print, it is the reaction: a beat off this base reclaims the 20-day at 37.10 and the 42.30 area where insiders were buying becomes the magnet.
recommendations.key_risk: Both insider anchors sit 15-18% underwater, so the smart money here has already been wrong for five months, and analyst revisions are still deteriorating (buy 12 to 8, sell 2 to 3 since June). If Monday brings another guidance cut, 35.22 goes and the next real support is untested — the stop at 34.60 is only 1.8% below the range low and an earnings gap can open straight through it, making the realised loss larger than the 2.50 risk stated.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is relative strength, and it is damning rather than merely weak: NKE is -50.91% against SPY over six months and still -1.73% against its own sector XLY over one month, so this is not a good business out of favour, it is a laggard among laggards. The answer is the structure of the trade, not a rebuttal of the fact — this is why the entry is conditional and above the market rather than a pullback bid. I am refusing to buy the decline at all; I only buy a reclaim of the 20-day that the print itself has to produce, which means the falling-knife scenario simply never fills me. The 42.30 target is also not a recovery call, it is five months back up the chart, well short of the 68.49 high.
